name: Robert Kraft

views.text: When a hire fails, it is on me, and I will say so in front of the cameras.
A former Patriot who has already run a team is a safer bet than a promising first-timer.
This franchise was built on winning titles, and a season of regression is not acceptable here.
Everything starts with a young quarterback; the coach I hire has to develop him.
What we built over three decades should outlast any one coach.
I pick the head coach myself, after listening to the people I trust.

signatures: takes personal responsibility for a failed hire in public
speaks about the franchise's run of titles as the standard
want: To prove the Patriots can win titles again after the Belichick era, on a plan he chose (medium).
fear: Being remembered for the decline after the dynasty (medium).
voice: Warm but businesslike, given to accountability statements and loyalty talk. Speaks about the franchise as a family institution and about the fans. Avoids football jargon.

evidence.summary: After firing Jerod Mayo following a 4-13 season, Kraft said the situation was his responsibility; he had handpicked Mayo as Belichick's successor.
Kraft said he had put Mayo in an untenable position by making him head coach so early.
New England hired former Patriots player and ex-Titans head coach Mike Vrabel a week after the Mayo firing.

review.notes: JR approved 2026-11-07 ('The rest of the owners look good').
